title: Effects of visualization of successful transcatheter aortic valve implantation on symptoms and quality of life – the VISUALIZE-TAVI study
summary: Aortic valve stenosis is one of the most common heart valve diseases in older people. Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) significantly improves the condition of many patients. But up to 40% of those treated report fewer improvements in their symptoms than expected medically after TAVI. Reasons for this may lie not only in the physical healing process, but also in how patients perceive the outcome of the treatment. The VISUALIZE-TAVI study aims to investigate whether providing patients with an image-based explanation after the procedure improves their perception of treatment success. To this end, some participants will be shown visual material to explain the results of the examination, such as before-and-after images showing the difference between the narrowed heart valve before the procedure and the new valve afterwards. The study will investigate whether visualisation influences symptoms, quality of life and motivation for active follow-up care.

interventions.name: Patients who, after successful TAVI, receive a paper printout of the initial aortic valve findings and the final intervention results with a layman's explanation of the success of the therapy from the Study Investigator.
Patients who, in accordance with standard clinical practice, receive the intervention findings in the form of a doctor's letter without visualization.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
    Symptomatic, severe aortic valve stenosis with indication for TAVI according to current guidelines (ESC, DGK) and in accordance with Heart Team consensus
     Willingness to participate voluntarily with a signed study informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
	Known pregnancy at the time of inclusion 
	EF < 35% 
	Severe, uncontrolled lung disease 
	Impaired vision 
	Impaired hearing
	Medications that affect the opioid system 
	Concomitant high-grade valve defect  
	Concomitant relevant coronary heart disease  
	Hb ≤ 7 g/dl 
	Participation in another interventional clinical trial 
	Life expectancy < 1 year due to a non-cardiac disease
	Cardiac amyloidosis
